# Images

PLL adds images to Python: you do not need to `import` anything to use them. If
a line in your file is an expression that produces an image, PLL shows it in the
interactions panel (and each picture there has a **Save SVG** button, if you want
to keep it). Each function below is shown with its contract (the types of its
inputs and output), followed by some examples and what they produce.

The type of an image, for type annotations, is `Image`:

```python
def bullseye(size: float) -> Image:
    """a red circle on top of a larger white one, on top of an even larger red one"""
    return overlay(circle(size, "solid", "red"),
                   circle(size * 2, "solid", "white"),
                   circle(size * 3, "solid", "red"))

bullseye(15)
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of bullseye(15)](/img/pll/images/0.svg)

</div>

In all of the functions below, a `mode` is either `"solid"` or `"outline"`, and a
`color` is a string naming a color, like `"red"` (see [Colors](#colors) for the
other ways to write colors). Sizes are in pixels, and can be `int`s or `float`s.

The pictures are drawn the way Racket's 2htdp/image library draws them: an
outline is a 1-pixel pen just inside the shape, so a shape is the same size
whether it is solid or outlined.

Every function checks what it is given, when it is called. A size that is text
or negative, a misspelled mode or color, a list where the images themselves
belong, or arguments in the wrong order each stop the program with a message
that names the argument:

```python error
rectangle(40, "solid", 20, "red")
```

<div className="pll-output">

```text
TypeError: rectangle's `height` (the 2nd argument) must be a number, but it is the string "solid". The arguments are: rectangle(width, height, mode, color).
```

</div>

```

```

A circle with the given radius.


### star

```
star(side: float, mode: str, color: str) -> Image
```

### star_polygon

```
star_polygon(side: float, points: int, step: int, mode: str, color: str) -> Image
```

A star with `points` points: it is made by drawing a line from each corner of a

```
line(dx: float, dy: float, color: str) -> Image
```

### text

```
text(string: str, size: float, color: str) -> Image
```

The string, written in letters `size` pixels tall. It is set in a monospace
font (every letter is the same width), so its width is exact, and its spaces are
kept.

```python

```

![Result of text('Hello', 24, 'olive')](/img/pll/images/20.svg)

</div>

```python

```

</div>

### empty_image

```
empty_image: Image
```

An image with nothing in it, 0 pixels wide and 0 pixels tall. Note that it is
not a function: write `empty_image`, not `empty_image()`. It's useful as a
starting point when you build up an image a piece at a time.

```python
image_width(empty_image)
```

<div className="pll-output">

```text
0
```

</div>

## Combining images

### beside

```
beside(image1: Image, image2: Image, ...) -> Image
```

The images next to each other, left to right, lined up along their centers. It
can be given any number of images.

```python
beside(ellipse(20, 70, "solid", "gray"),
       ellipse(20, 50, "solid", "darkgray"),
       ellipse(20, 30, "solid", "dimgray"),
       ellipse(20, 10, "solid", "black"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of beside(ellipse(20, 70, 'solid', 'gray'), ellipse(20, 50, 'solid', 'darkgray'), ellipse(20, 30, 'solid', 'dimgray'), ellipse(20, 10, 'solid', 'black'))](/img/pll/images/23.svg)

</div>

### above

```
above(image1: Image, image2: Image, ...) -> Image
```

The images stacked, with `image1` on top, lined up along their centers. It can
be given any number of images.

```python
above(ellipse(70, 20, "solid", "gray"),
      ellipse(50, 20, "solid", "darkgray"),
      ellipse(30, 20, "solid", "dimgray"),
      ellipse(10, 20, "solid", "black"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of above(ellipse(70, 20, 'solid', 'gray'), ellipse(50, 20, 'solid', 'darkgray'), ellipse(30, 20, 'solid', 'dimgray'), ellipse(10, 20, 'solid', 'black'))](/img/pll/images/24.svg)

</div>

### overlay

```
overlay(image1: Image, image2: Image, ...) -> Image
```

The images on top of each other, with their centers lined up, and `image1` on
top. (So if `image1` is bigger than the others, they can't be seen!) It can be
given any number of images.

```python
overlay(rectangle(30, 60, "solid", "orange"),
        ellipse(60, 30, "solid", "purple"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of overlay(rectangle(30, 60, 'solid', 'orange'), ellipse(60, 30, 'solid', 'purple'))](/img/pll/images/25.svg)

</div>

```python
overlay(ellipse(10, 10, "solid", "red"),
        ellipse(20, 20, "solid", "black"),
        ellipse(30, 30, "solid", "red"),
        ellipse(40, 40, "solid", "black"),
        ellipse(50, 50, "solid", "red"),
        ellipse(60, 60, "solid", "black"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of ellipse(60, 60, 'solid', 'black'))](/img/pll/images/26.svg)

</div>

### underlay

```
underlay(image1: Image, image2: Image, ...) -> Image
```

Like `overlay`, but with `image1` on the bottom.

```python
underlay(rectangle(30, 60, "solid", "orange"),
         ellipse(60, 30, "solid", "purple"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of underlay(rectangle(30, 60, 'solid', 'orange'), ellipse(60, 30, 'solid', 'purple'))](/img/pll/images/27.svg)

</div>

## Lining up edges

These work like the functions above, but their first input(s) say which edges of
the images line up. A horizontal place (`x_place`) is `"left"`, `"center"`, or
`"right"`, and a vertical place (`y_place`) is `"top"`, `"center"`, or
`"bottom"`.

### beside_align

```
beside_align(y_place: str, image1: Image, image2: Image, ...) -> Image
```

Like `beside`, but lined up at the `y_place` edge.

```python
beside_align("bottom",
             ellipse(20, 70, "solid", "lightsteelblue"),
             ellipse(20, 50, "solid", "mediumslateblue"),
             ellipse(20, 30, "solid", "slateblue"),
             ellipse(20, 10, "solid", "navy"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of ellipse(20, 10, 'solid', 'navy'))](/img/pll/images/28.svg)

</div>

```python
beside_align("top",
             ellipse(20, 70, "solid", "mediumorchid"),
             ellipse(20, 50, "solid", "darkorchid"),
             ellipse(20, 30, "solid", "purple"),
             ellipse(20, 10, "solid", "indigo"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of ellipse(20, 10, 'solid', 'indigo'))](/img/pll/images/29.svg)

</div>

### above_align

```
above_align(x_place: str, image1: Image, image2: Image, ...) -> Image
```

Like `above`, but lined up at the `x_place` edge.

```python
above_align("right",
            ellipse(70, 20, "solid", "gold"),
            ellipse(50, 20, "solid", "goldenrod"),
            ellipse(30, 20, "solid", "darkgoldenrod"),
            ellipse(10, 20, "solid", "sienna"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of ellipse(10, 20, 'solid', 'sienna'))](/img/pll/images/30.svg)

</div>

```python
above_align("left",
            ellipse(70, 20, "solid", "yellowgreen"),
            ellipse(50, 20, "solid", "olivedrab"),
            ellipse(30, 20, "solid", "darkolivegreen"),
            ellipse(10, 20, "solid", "darkgreen"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of ellipse(10, 20, 'solid', 'darkgreen'))](/img/pll/images/31.svg)

</div>

### overlay_align

```
overlay_align(x_place: str, y_place: str, image1: Image, image2: Image, ...) -> Image
```

Like `overlay`, but lined up at the `x_place` and `y_place` edges: e.g.,
`"right", "bottom"` puts the images' bottom right corners together.

```python
overlay_align("left", "center",
              rectangle(30, 60, "solid", "orange"),
              ellipse(60, 30, "solid", "purple"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of overlay_align('left', 'center', rectangle(30, 60, 'solid', 'orange'), ellipse(60, 30, 'solid', 'purple'))](/img/pll/images/32.svg)

</div>

```python
overlay_align("right", "bottom",
              rectangle(20, 20, "solid", "silver"),
              rectangle(30, 30, "solid", "seagreen"),
              rectangle(40, 40, "solid", "silver"),
              rectangle(50, 50, "solid", "seagreen"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of rectangle(50, 50, 'solid', 'seagreen'))](/img/pll/images/33.svg)

</div>

### underlay_align

```
underlay_align(x_place: str, y_place: str, image1: Image, image2: Image, ...) -> Image
```

Like `overlay_align`, but with `image1` on the bottom.

```python
underlay_align("right", "top",
               rectangle(50, 50, "solid", "seagreen"),
               rectangle(40, 40, "solid", "silver"),
               rectangle(30, 30, "solid", "seagreen"),
               rectangle(20, 20, "solid", "silver"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of rectangle(20, 20, 'solid', 'silver'))](/img/pll/images/34.svg)

## Placing images exactly

### overlay_xy

```
overlay_xy(image1: Image, dx: float, dy: float, image2: Image) -> Image
```

`image1` on top of `image2`, with `image2` moved `dx` pixels to the right and `dy`
pixels down from `image1`'s top left corner. Negative numbers move it left or up.
The result is as big as it needs to be to hold both images: nothing is cut off.

```python
overlay_xy(rectangle(20, 20, "outline", "black"),
           20, 0,
           rectangle(20, 20, "outline", "black"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of overlay_xy(rectangle(20, 20, 'outline', 'black'), 20, 0, rectangle(20, 20, 'outline', 'black'))](/img/pll/images/35.svg)

</div>

```python
overlay_xy(rectangle(20, 20, "solid", "red"),
           10, 10,
           rectangle(20, 20, "solid", "black"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of overlay_xy(rectangle(20, 20, 'solid', 'red'), 10, 10, rectangle(20, 20, 'solid', 'black'))](/img/pll/images/36.svg)

</div>

```python
overlay_xy(rectangle(20, 20, "solid", "red"),
           -10, -10,
           rectangle(20, 20, "solid", "black"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of overlay_xy(rectangle(20, 20, 'solid', 'red'), -10, -10, rectangle(20, 20, 'solid', 'black'))](/img/pll/images/37.svg)

</div>

### underlay_xy

```
underlay_xy(image1: Image, dx: float, dy: float, image2: Image) -> Image
```

Like `overlay_xy`, but with `image1` on the bottom.

```python
underlay_xy(rectangle(20, 20, "solid", "red"),
            10, 10,
            rectangle(20, 20, "solid", "black"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of underlay_xy(rectangle(20, 20, 'solid', 'red'), 10, 10, rectangle(20, 20, 'solid', 'black'))](/img/pll/images/38.svg)

</div>

## Scenes

A scene is a fixed-size canvas, which is useful for drawing the frames of an
[animation](/pll/reactors). In a scene (and in images in general), the point
`(0, 0)` is the **top left** corner: increasing `x` moves right, and increasing
`y` moves **down**.

### empty_scene

```
empty_scene(width: float, height: float) -> Image
```

An empty, white scene that is `width` wide and `height` tall, with a thin
outline.

```python
empty_scene(160, 90)
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of empty_scene(160, 90)](/img/pll/images/39.svg)

</div>

### place_image

```
place_image(image: Image, x: float, y: float, scene: Image) -> Image
```

`scene`, with `image` placed so that its **center** is at `(x, y)`. Unlike
`overlay_xy`, the result is the same size as `scene`: anything that goes past its
edges is cut off.

```python
place_image(triangle(32, "solid", "red"), 24, 24, empty_scene(48, 48))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of place_image(triangle(32, 'solid', 'red'), 24, 24, empty_scene(48, 48))](/img/pll/images/40.svg)

</div>

```python
place_image(circle(8, "solid", "tomato"), 0, 0, empty_scene(48, 48))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of place_image(circle(8, 'solid', 'tomato'), 0, 0, empty_scene(48, 48))](/img/pll/images/41.svg)

</div>

```python
place_image(circle(4, "solid", "white"), 18, 6,
            place_image(circle(4, "solid", "white"), 0, 6,
                        place_image(circle(4, "solid", "white"), 14, 32,
                                    rectangle(48, 48, "solid", "navy"))))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of place_image(circle(4, 'solid', 'white'), 18, 6, place_image(circle(4, 'solid', 'white'), 0, 6, place_image(circle(4, 'solid', 'white'), 14, 32, rectangle(48, 48, 'solid', 'navy'))))](/img/pll/images/42.svg)

</div>

### crop

```
crop(x: float, y: float, width: float, height: float, image: Image) -> Image
```

The `width` by `height` piece of `image` whose top left corner is at `(x, y)`.


## Transforming images

### rotate

```
rotate(angle: float, image: Image) -> Image
```

`image`, turned `angle` degrees counter-clockwise (or clockwise, if `angle` is
negative). The result is as big as it needs to be to hold the turned shapes, so a
circle turned is as wide as it was. The angle comes first:

```python error
rotate(square(20, "solid", "red"), 45)
```

<div className="pll-output">

```text
TypeError: rotate takes the `angle` first, then the image: write rotate(45, image).
```

</div>

```python
rotate(45, ellipse(60, 20, "solid", "olivedrab"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of rotate(45, ellipse(60, 20, 'solid', 'olivedrab'))](/img/pll/images/47.svg)

</div>

```python
rotate(5, rectangle(50, 50, "outline", "black"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of rotate(5, rectangle(50, 50, 'outline', 'black'))](/img/pll/images/48.svg)

</div>

```python
rotate(-90, triangle(40, "solid", "seagreen"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of rotate(-90, triangle(40, 'solid', 'seagreen'))](/img/pll/images/49.svg)

</div>

### scale

```
scale(factor: float, image: Image) -> Image
```

`image`, made `factor` times as big: e.g., `2` is twice as wide and twice as
tall, and `0.5` is half as wide and half as tall.

```python
scale(2, ellipse(20, 30, "solid", "blue"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of scale(2, ellipse(20, 30, 'solid', 'blue'))](/img/pll/images/50.svg)

</div>

```python
scale(0.5, ellipse(20, 30, "solid", "blue"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of scale(0.5, ellipse(20, 30, 'solid', 'blue'))](/img/pll/images/51.svg)

</div>

### flip_horizontal

```
flip_horizontal(image: Image) -> Image
```

`image`, mirrored left to right.

```python
beside(rotate(30, square(50, "solid", "red")),
       flip_horizontal(rotate(30, square(50, "solid", "blue"))))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of beside(rotate(30, square(50, 'solid', 'red')), flip_horizontal(rotate(30, square(50, 'solid', 'blue'))))](/img/pll/images/52.svg)

</div>

### flip_vertical

```
flip_vertical(image: Image) -> Image
```

`image`, mirrored top to bottom.

```python

```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of above(star(40, 'solid', 'firebrick'), scale(0.5, flip_vertical(star(40, 'solid', 'gray'))))](/img/pll/images/53.svg)

## Comparing images

Two images are `==` when they draw the same shapes, in the same places, in the
same colors, however they were made, so `"red"` and `(255, 0, 0)` are the same
color:

```python
circle(20, "solid", "red") == circle(20, "solid", (255, 0, 0))
```

<div className="pll-output">

```text
True
```

</div>

```python
beside(square(10, "solid", "red"), square(10, "solid", "blue")) == beside(square(10, "solid", "blue"), square(10, "solid", "red"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

```text
False
```

</div>

So you can test a function that draws something by comparing what it draws with
the image it should draw:

```python
def dot(r: float) -> Image:
    """a red dot of radius r"""
    return circle(r, "solid", "red")

def test_dot():
    assert dot(3) == circle(3, "solid", "red")
    assert image_width(dot(5)) == 10
```

## Loading pictures

### load_image

```
load_image(source: str) -> Image
```

A picture, read from a file in the same folder as your program (when `source` is
a file name, like `"cat.png"`), or from an address on the web (when `source`
starts with `https://`). It gives you an ordinary image, so everything above
works on it. PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, and SVG files are understood, up to 2 MB each:
these are for the graphics a program draws with, not for photographs.

```python
doghouse = load_image("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neu-pdi/cs2000-public-resources/refs/heads/main/static/img/lab5-doghouse.png")
scale(0.25, doghouse)
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of doghouse = load_image('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neu-pdi/cs2000-public-resources/refs/heads/main/static/img/lab5-doghouse.png') scale(0.25, doghouse)](/img/pll/images/61.svg)

</div>

```python
beside(scale(0.2, doghouse), scale(0.2, flip_horizontal(doghouse)))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of beside(scale(0.2, doghouse), scale(0.2, flip_horizontal(doghouse)))](/img/pll/images/62.svg)

</div>

In the browser, an address on the web only works if its site allows other sites
to read it. If loading fails, download the picture, add it to your repository
(next to your program), and load it by its file name instead.

## Colors

A color can be:

- the name of a color, like `"red"`, `"navy"`, or `"gold"` (any [CSS color
  name](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/named-color) works,
  and so does `"transparent"`);
- a hex code, like `"#ff8800"` or `"#f80"`;
- `"rgb(255, 136, 0)"` or `"hsl(32, 100%, 50%)"`, or `"rgba(...)"` and
  `"hsla(...)"` with a fourth number from `0.0` to `1.0` saying how solid it is;
- a tuple `(red, green, blue)`, with each from 0 to 255, like `(255, 136, 0)`;
- a tuple `(red, green, blue, alpha)`, where `alpha` says how solid the color is:
  a whole number from `0` (invisible) to `255` (solid), or a fraction from `0.0`
  to `1.0`, so `(255, 0, 0, 128)` and `(255, 0, 0, 0.5)` are both half
  see-through.

A color name is checked against the CSS names, so a misspelled one stops the
program and suggests the name you meant, rather than drawing nothing:

```python error
circle(20, "solid", "bleu")
```

<div className="pll-output">

```text
ValueError: circle's `color` (the 3rd argument) is the string "bleu", which is not a color name PLL knows. Did you mean "blue"?
```

</div>

```python
beside(circle(20, "solid", "darkorange"),
       circle(20, "solid", "#ff8800"),
       circle(20, "solid", (255, 136, 0)))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of beside(circle(20, 'solid', 'darkorange'), circle(20, 'solid', '#ff8800'), circle(20, 'solid', (255, 136, 0)))](/img/pll/images/64.svg)

</div>

```python
overlay(circle(20, "solid", (0, 0, 255, 0.5)),
        rectangle(60, 20, "solid", "gold"))
```

<div className="pll-output">

![Result of overlay(circle(20, 'solid', (0, 0, 255, 0.5)), rectangle(60, 20, 'solid', 'gold'))](/img/pll/images/65.svg)

</div>
